cases.purpose: The destination PATH is a non-empty directory, so the final rename of the temp file fails (EISDIR) without any injection: index write fails with a diagnostic, the directory and its member are untouched, PATH.lock and PATH.tmp* are removed, and a write after the directory is removed succeeds.
cases.oracle: The documented atomic-replacement contract of index write (help: 'Atomic write'; _git/index.c mkstemp, write loop, fdatasync, close, rename) and git's lock semantics: on any failure the destination keeps its previous state, PATH.lock and PATH.tmp* are removed, the status is 1 with a diagnostic, and a later write succeeds. Expected listing is the independently written entries in index read's 'mode sha stage path' form. setup_script proves with Python that rename(file, non-empty directory) fails EISDIR and keeps both.
cases.comparison: Exact status, diagnostic presence, destination directory and member intact, residue count, recovery status and listing.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t index) == builtin ]] || { printf 'candidate index builtin missing\n'; exit 99; }
printf '100644 2222222222222222222222222222222222222222 0\tbeta\n100755 3333333333333333333333333333333333333333 0\tgamma\n' > e2
/usr/bin/mkdir -p w/idx; printf 'keep\n' > w/idx/occupant
index write w/idx < e2 2> "$HOME/err.rename-dir"; rc=$?
[[ -s $HOME/err.rename-dir ]] && d=yes || d=no
[[ -d w/idx && $(< w/idx/occupant) == keep && $(/usr/bin/ls -A w/idx) == occupant ]] && dest=directory-intact || dest=changed
n=0; for f in w/* w/.[!.]*; do [[ -e $f && ${f##*/} != idx ]] && n=$((n + 1)); done
printf 'fault=rename-onto-dir rc=%d diag=%s dest=%s residue=%d\n' "$rc" "$d" "$dest" "$n"
/usr/bin/rm -rf w/idx
index write w/idx < e2; printf 'recovery=%d\n' "$?"
index read w/idx
/usr/bin/rm -rf w e2

cases.purpose: After an output failure (stdout is /dev/full) while the first operand is still being processed, the later operand, which exists, is never opened: the openat log of the whole command shows the first operand opened and the later one not.
cases.oracle: GNU coreutils 9.7 unexpand under the identical seccomp notify filter (openat paths logged, every call continued); unexpand exits on the first write error before advancing to the next operand. setup_script proves /dev/full gives ENOSPC and that a Python open under the identical filter appears in the log.
cases.comparison: Exact status, diagnostic presence and per-path openat observations (first operand opened, later operand not).

files.opened.py:
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# Report whether each NAME appears as the path of a logged openat in a
# system-seccomp.py notify log (one JSON object per call).
import json, sys
log, names = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2:]
paths = set()
for line in open(log):
    if line.strip():
        r = json.loads(line)
        if r.get("syscall") == "openat":
            paths.update(str(v) for k, v in r.items() if k.startswith("string"))
print(" ".join("%s=%s" % (n, "yes" if n in paths else "no") for n in names))

cases.setup_script:
: > "$HOME/control.txt"
/usr/bin/python3 -I control.py devfull >> "$HOME/control.txt"
: > probe.txt
/usr/bin/python3 /opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/system-seccomp.py --notify openat --log-string openat=1 --log "$HOME/control.jsonl" -- /usr/bin/python3 -I "$PWD/control.py" open probe.txt >> "$HOME/control.txt"
[[ $(/usr/bin/python3 -I opened.py "$HOME/control.jsonl" probe.txt) == probe.txt=yes ]]
printf 'log: control open of probe.txt recorded\n' >> "$HOME/control.txt"
/usr/bin/rm -f probe.txt
cases.script:
/usr/bin/yes '        x' | /usr/bin/head -c 1048576 > big
printf '        y\n' > later-present
/usr/bin/python3 /opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/system-seccomp.py --notify openat --log-string openat=1 --log "$HOME/open.jsonl" -- "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c 'unexpand big later-present > /dev/full; printf "%d" "$?" > "$HOME/rc.full"' 2> "$HOME/err.full"
[[ -s $HOME/err.full ]] && d=yes || d=no
printf 'enospc rc=%s diag=%s\n' "$(< "$HOME/rc.full")" "$d"
printf 'opened %s\n' "$(/usr/bin/python3 -I opened.py "$HOME/open.jsonl" big later-present)"
/usr/bin/rm -f big later-present
cases.stdout:
enospc rc=1 diag=yes
opened big=yes later-present=no

cases.purpose: Invalid ACL text (bad permission letter, unknown tag, unknown user, missing permissions, empty spec, -x with permissions, a list mixing valid and invalid entries), unknown options and missing or absent file operands are refused without changing the ACL; '--' ends option parsing so '-b' and '-x' after it are file operands.
cases.oracle: GNU acl setfacl on tmpfs files owned by uid 2000 in the initial user namespace; the trusted GNU getfacl -n reads both files on both sides after every step. setup_script proves tmpfs ACL support with GNU setfacl/getfacl.
cases.comparison: Exact per-step status, diagnostic presence, octal modes and getfacl listings of both files; identical tree.
cases.setup_script:
: > "$HOME/control.txt"
: > "$HOME/acl-probe"
/usr/bin/setfacl -m u:2001:r "$HOME/acl-probe"
/usr/bin/getfacl -n "$HOME/acl-probe" 2> /dev/null | /usr/bin/grep -qx 'user:2001:r--'
/usr/bin/rm "$HOME/acl-probe"
printf 'acl: named user entry stored and read back on tmpfs\n' >> "$HOME/control.txt"
cases.script:
umask 022
: > f; : > ./-b
setfacl -m u:2001:rw f || exit 98
show() { printf '%s mode=%s\n' "$1" "$(/usr/bin/stat -c %a -- "$1")"; /usr/bin/getfacl -n --absolute-names -- "$1"; }
step() {
  local label=$1; shift
  eval "setfacl $*" < /dev/null 2> "$HOME/err.$label"; local rc=$?
  [[ -s $HOME/err.$label ]] && d=yes || d=no
  printf '== %s rc=%d diag=%s\n' "$label" "$rc" "$d"
  show f; show -b
}
step invalid-perm -m u:2001:rwz f
step invalid-tag -m x:2001:r f
step unknown-user -m u:no_such_user_zz:r f
step missing-perms -m u:2001 f
step empty-spec -m "''" f
step remove-with-perms -x u:2001:r f
step remove-absent-entry -x u:2009 f
step mixed-valid-invalid -m u:2002:r,u:2003:q f
step unknown-option -Z f
step no-file-operand -m u:2002:r
step missing-file -m u:2002:r nofile
step dashdash-file -m u:2002:r -- -b
step dashdash-only-file -m u:2002:rw -- f
step option-after-dashdash -m u:2004:r -- -b -x
/usr/bin/rm -f f ./-b

cases.purpose: A named operand that opens as a regular file but whose first read fails with EIO (/proc/self/mem at offset 0, reported S_ISREG with st_size 0) prints no checksum and a diagnostic; the operands before and after it are still checksummed and the status is 1.
cases.oracle: GNU coreutils 9.7 sha256sum on the same operands (each side reads its own process's /proc/self/mem); expected digest of 'second\n' computed independently. setup_script proves with Python that /proc/self/mem opens, is S_ISREG and fails the first read with EIO.
cases.comparison: Exact stdout lines, status, diagnostic presence and absence of a /proc/self/mem line.
cases.script:
printf 'second\n' > file2
sha256sum file2 /proc/self/mem file2 > out 2> "$HOME/err.mem"; rc=$?
[[ -s $HOME/err.mem ]] && d=yes || d=no
printf '%s\n' "$(< out)"
/usr/bin/grep -q 'proc/self/mem' out && m=present || m=absent
printf 'rc=%d diag=%s mem-line=%s\n' "$rc" "$d" "$m"
/usr/bin/rm -f out file2
